chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to ride upon red velvet.

key_terms.حَمْرَاء: Red (feminine form); refers to the color of the riding cloth
key_terms.قَطِيفَة: A thick, plush or velvet-like cloth; used as a saddle cloth or riding cover

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Zayn al-Abidin ride on red velvet? What does al-Kafi say about the Imam's riding practice?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reports that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, peace be upon him) used to ride on a saddle cloth or covering made of red velvet. This hadith documents a detail of the fourth Imam's personal conduct and customary practice, serving as a precedent for the permissibility of using red-colored fabric and plush materials for riding. In the early Shia community, such biographical reports about the Imams were valued as normative guides for everyday permissibility.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Yahya Al Madainy,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was riding upon red velvet’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Hashim from Ibrahim ibn abu Yahya al-Madiniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, rode on a piece of marigold red color cloth.’
